_comment: This file is the ONLY place these regexes are written. Three runtimes read
it, so it is data rather than code:
The agent image is built from a SEPARATE Docker context (infra/agent-image),
so build-and-push.sh stages this exact committed file into
`source` must be valid in BOTH JavaScript and Python `re` — no named groups,
no lookbehind, no \p{...}. Matching is always done case-insensitively and
globally by each loader; flags are deliberately not stored here.

patterns.description: PSD student numbers: 7 digits starting with 2 (e.g. 2240393)
US phone with country code, unpunctuated

_policy_comment: publicFileMinDistinct — how many DISTINCT matched values of a kind make a
text-extractable file unfit for a public link.
1  An identifier that is personal on its own. A single student number or
SSN in a file means that file is about a person.
2  A contact detail that public district content legitimately carries ONE
of: the school phone number in a flyer footer, a department address on
a job posting, the author's own signature line. TWO or more distinct
ones is a contact list, which is what #1886 found on public links
The narration policy (psd-tts) deliberately does NOT use these thresholds:
_narration_policy_comment: Narration (psd-tts) refuses on the FIRST match of any kind.
Audio cannot be checked after the fact — `psd-tts` uploads every MP3
public-by-link (for 30 days, like any public artifact), and once synthesised
the bytes are opaque audio that no later text check, including the
broker's public-link scan, can read. There is also no
legitimate reason to speak a phone number or an address into a shareable
recording: the agent can say "call the front office" and lose nothing. So
the cheap, strict rule applies here and the flyer-footer allowance does not.
